title: lookup/len/snapshot report expired leases as live
description:
File: rust/lichen-rpl/src/address_assignment.rs
Perspective: correctness

prune_expired() is invoked from build(), process(), and handle_dao(). lookup_by_short(), lookup_by_eui(), expires_at(), len(), is_empty(), and snapshot() do not prune.

After a lease deadline passes, lookup_by_short still returns the EUI, len() still counts it, and snapshot() still includes it, while expires_at() already reports a deadline in the past. The lookup docs say currently owns; expired rows do not currently own. A caller using lookup_by_short for L2 resolution will keep mapping traffic to a lapsed lease until an unrelated process()/prune_expired() runs.

Fix: have the read APIs prune (or answer from a view that excludes deadline <= now) so lookup/len/snapshot and process() observe the same table. expires_at() can still return the stored deadline after prune (None).
